item.title: Neural Route Mapping Cuts Simulated Industrial IoT Network Delay by 28 Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Industrial environments across high-growth construction and manufacturing sectors generate massive volumes of critical telemetry, including toxic gas sensor alerts, operational heat signals, structural stress indications, and wearable health measurements.
  • In the context of national infrastructure projects such as those expanding across Saudi Arabia, legacy cellular deployments frequently falter under heavy local traffic spikes or physical spectrum exhaustion.
  • Individual per-hop delays incorporate medium access intervals, Shannon transmission durations, and relay buffer holding times, allowing the researcher to aggregate hop latencies across full multi-hop trajectories into mathematically closed end-to-end delay formulations.

본문

A mathematical modeling and analytical simulation study published in the Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Engineering and Architecture demonstrates that combining a Neural Route Mapping Protocol with Voronoi cell geometric partitioning and conflict-graph scheduling significantly improves communication efficiency across dense industrial monitoring systems. Conducted by researcher Abdulfattah Noorwali, the theoretical framework evaluates an Industrial Internet of Things architecture tailored to high-density environments, addressing performance collapse caused by radio interference, queueing buildup, and spectrum contention during safety emergencies. Analytical predictions paired with simulation scenarios show that the integrated protocol yields an estimated 45 to 55 percent aggregate throughput increase alongside a 60 to 75 percent reduction in transmission packet losses when evaluated against standard Dynamic Source Routing baselines.

Industrial environments across high-growth construction and manufacturing sectors generate massive volumes of critical telemetry, including toxic gas sensor alerts, operational heat signals, structural stress indications, and wearable health measurements. In the context of national infrastructure projects such as those expanding across Saudi Arabia, legacy cellular deployments frequently falter under heavy local traffic spikes or physical spectrum exhaustion. Radio signals across industrial installations encounter severe metal reflections and high spatial device concentration, causing primary conflicts where nodes attempt concurrent transmission and reception, as well as secondary conflicts arising from adjacent transmitter overlap. The resulting data collisions and multi-hop delivery delays risk blocking life-saving alerts, requiring dedicated low-power frameworks that provide mathematically verifiable, bounded delays rather than purely empirical routing heuristics.

To solve these transmission bottlenecks, the research develops a unified three-tier communication hierarchy comprising distributed end sensor nodes, intermediate multi-hop relay routers, and central gateways. Low-power sensor nodes continuously collect environmental observations and associate directly with the closest relay router through a planar Voronoi tessellation that creates non-overlapping coverage zones. These multi-hop relay routers communicate using Long Range radio frequencies to forward aggregated packets across directed network graphs toward control-node gateways. The study analytically defines propagation conditions using a log-normal shadowing path-loss model with typical industrial path-loss exponents ranging from 3 to 4, establishing explicit signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio feasibility thresholds to guarantee reliable physical-layer decoding across interfering radio links.

item.title: Predictive Edge-IoT Solar Framework Stows Arrays and Shields Panels Against Hail - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Engineers have developed an edge-computing internet-of-things framework that combines machine learning weather forecasting with automated mechanical defenses to protect decentralized solar arrays from severe wind and hail while boosting annual energy yield.
  • In a study published in Results in Engineering, a research team designed and computationally evaluated a dual-mode mechanism governed by an ESP32 microcontroller running localized machine learning algorithms.
  • The system addresses a fundamental vulnerability in conventional fixed-tilt rooftop and decentralized solar photovoltaic installations, which remain permanently static and passively exposed to extreme meteorological hazards.

본문

Engineers have developed an edge-computing internet-of-things framework that combines machine learning weather forecasting with automated mechanical defenses to protect decentralized solar arrays from severe wind and hail while boosting annual energy yield. In a study published in Results in Engineering, a research team designed and computationally evaluated a dual-mode mechanism governed by an ESP32 microcontroller running localized machine learning algorithms. The system addresses a fundamental vulnerability in conventional fixed-tilt rooftop and decentralized solar photovoltaic installations, which remain permanently static and passively exposed to extreme meteorological hazards. Standard installations typically endure high drag forces when buffeted by gale-force winds and face severe cracking of tempered front glass during kinetic macro-hail impacts. By transitioning solar infrastructure from reactive sensor overrides to pre-emptive predictive actuation, the new framework autonomously shifts panels into defensive postures prior to storm arrival.

The engineering challenge stems directly from the mechanical limits of conventional decentralized photovoltaics. Standard solar installations are conventionally oriented at fixed operating tilts of approximately 30 degrees to optimize daylight solar radiation capture. At these steep inclinations, solar arrays act as bluff bodies within turbulent boundary layer flows, accumulating severe aerodynamic drag and upward lift that can exceed the structural tolerances of mounting frames and lead to catastrophic structural collapse. Concurrently, severe convective storm cells generate kinetic impacts from macro-hail that easily shatter standard tempered solar glass. While utility-scale facilities sometimes use slow tracking overrides, standard residential and off-grid decentralized arrays completely lack the mechanical kinematics required to execute protective maneuvers. The traditional industrial approach to hail vulnerability has relied on manufacturing panels with thicker, heavier glass layers, but that passive strategy increases hardware costs, adds physical mass to mounting structures, and degrades solar transmittance, which permanently diminishes long-term electrical generation efficiency.

item.title: SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handov - Hackster.io
item.description:
요약

  • SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handover via oneM2M (ACME CSE) Over Private 5G
  • SwarmLink-M2M solves this challenge by establishing the oneM2M Common Services Entity (CSE), specifically the ACME CSE reference platform, as the single authoritative source of truth, security arbiter, and coordination backbone for an entire autonomous swarm.
  • 1. Clause 7.1 (Custom MEC-IPE Telemetry Architecture): Ingests real-time 5G RAN and Core radio parameters (RSRP, SINR, CQI, MCS, BLER) directly into standard oneM2M flexContainer resources ([custom:mecRadioInfo]) over the Mca reference point.

본문

SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handover via oneM2M (ACME CSE) Over Private 5G

Modern mission-critical environments (ranging from automated manufacturing floors to hazardous emergency response zones) rely on fleets of heterogeneous IoT sensors and mobile autonomous robots. However, conventional multi-agent deployments suffer from severe architectural fragmentation: they rely on fragile peer-to-peer ad-hoc messaging, unstandardized proprietary message brokers, or centralized cloud platforms that fail when connectivity drops or when mobile robots traverse radio cell boundaries.

SwarmLink-M2M solves this challenge by establishing the oneM2M Common Services Entity (CSE), specifically the ACME CSE reference platform, as the single authoritative source of truth, security arbiter, and coordination backbone for an entire autonomous swarm. Operating over an on-premise Private 5G Standalone (SA) network with Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), SwarmLink-M2M coordinates stationary ESP32 sensor swarm nodes and a mobile Raspberry Pi 5 "Robot Doctor".

Our project addresses four critical standardization frontiers in ETSI TR-0077 (MEC Interworking & Swarm Computing):

1. Clause 7.1 (Custom MEC-IPE Telemetry Architecture): Ingests real-time 5G RAN and Core radio parameters (RSRP, SINR, CQI, MCS, BLER) directly into standard oneM2M flexContainer resources ([custom:mecRadioInfo]) over the Mca reference point.

2. Clause 7.2 (Signal-Triggered Inter-MN-CSE Handover): Implements an autonomous IN-CSE Handover Orchestrator actor that triggers seamless cross-district re-registration of mobile Application Entities (RobotAE) when signal quality drops, measuring application-layer interruption time (Delta t).

3. Clause 7.4 (Swarm Computing Resource Definitions): Formally contributes concrete oneM2M resource definitions for swarm coordination: [swarmMembership], [swarmTask], and [swarmContext].

4. Clause 7.3 & TS-0043 (Federated Learning Lifecycle & Model Management): Manages distributed edge model rounds ([flOperation], [flRound], [modelVersion]) and deploys updated anomaly detection models via oneM2M software management ([mgmtObj]).

When building an industrial monitoring system, the typical path of least resistance is to deploy an MQTT broker or a proprietary cloud database, write custom client scripts, and bolt on a user interface. If a standard like oneM2M is included at all, it often ends up as a passive telemetry sink: if the CSE crashes, the rest of the application continues without interruption.

Our project began with a deliberate decision to reject this superficial integration. We asked ourselves a fundamental question: What happens if you remove the CSE? If the answer is that the system still functions, then oneM2M is merely decorative. We set out to build an architecture where oneM2M is indispensable: remove the CSE, and the entire system stops.

item.title: IOTek, 2026년 베트남 디지털 기술 기업 톱 10 진입 예정 - Vietnam.vn
item.description:
요약

  • 이번 시상식은 베트남 과학기술부 의 후원 아래 베트남 소프트웨어 및 정보기술 서비스 협회(VINASA)가 주최한 '베트남 톱 10 테크 & 맵 2026' 프로그램의 일환으로 11월 18일에 개최되었습니다.
  • IOTek은 스마트 인프라를 위한 통합 사물 인터넷(IoT) 및 인공지능( AI ) 솔루션 연구 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.
  • IOTek은 이러한 기술 플랫폼을 기반으로 지능형 주차장 관리 솔루션인 Smart Parking, 건설 현장의 출입 통제를 지원하는 SiteGate, AI 카메라 시스템, 출입 통제 및 도시 지역 운영 관리와 같은 특수 솔루션을 개발합니다.

본문

이번 시상식은 베트남 과학기술부 의 후원 아래 베트남 소프트웨어 및 정보기술 서비스 협회(VINASA)가 주최한 '베트남 톱 10 테크 & 맵 2026' 프로그램의 일환으로 11월 18일에 개최되었습니다.

이는 One Mount 디지털 생태계 내의 기술 기업인 IOTek에게 중요한 이정표입니다. IOTek은 스마트 인프라를 위한 통합 사물 인터넷(IoT) 및 인공지능( AI ) 솔루션 연구 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.

“베트남 톱 10 테크 & 맵 2026에 선정된 것은 아이오텍 팀의 기술력과 노력을 인정받은 고무적인 일입니다. 이는 앞으로도 사물인터넷(IoT) 및 인공지능(AI) 솔루션 연구 개발에 지속적으로 투자하여 운영 효율성을 향상시키고 베트남의 스마트 인프라 발전을 촉진하는 데 더욱 매진할 수 있도록 동기를 부여합니다.”라고 아이오텍 이사회 의장인 응우옌 당 쭝(Nguyen Dang Trung) 씨는 밝혔습니다.

2025년 8월에 설립된 IOTek의 제품 포트폴리오는 크게 세 가지 솔루션 그룹으로 구성됩니다. 여기에는 디바이스 연결 플랫폼인 IoT 플랫폼, 스마트 관리 및 운영 플랫폼, 그리고 AI 애플리케이션 및 IoT 엣지 프로세싱 디바이스가 포함됩니다.

특히, AIoT 플랫폼은 IOTek이 개발한 지능형 관리 및 운영 플랫폼으로, 도시 지역, 건물, 병원, 공항 및 건설 현장의 응용 분야를 목표로 합니다.

이 플랫폼은 다양한 장치의 데이터를 단일 시스템 내에서 연결, 수집 및 중앙 집중식으로 관리할 수 있도록 지원하며, 연중무휴 24시간 보안 모니터링, 실시간 데이터 처리 및 운영 프로세스 자동화를 제공합니다. 허브-엣지 아키텍처를 기반으로 하는 AIoT 플랫폼은 여러 공급업체의 장치를 통합할 수 있으며, 네트워크 연결이 중단되더라도 배포 지점에서 지속적인 운영을 보장합니다.

IOTek은 이러한 기술 플랫폼을 기반으로 지능형 주차장 관리 솔루션인 Smart Parking, 건설 현장의 출입 통제를 지원하는 SiteGate, AI 카메라 시스템, 출입 통제 및 도시 지역 운영 관리와 같은 특수 솔루션을 개발합니다.

이러한 솔루션들은 이미 실제 현장에서 적용되어 구체적인 성과를 거두고 있습니다. 하노이 의 고층 아파트 단지에서는 스마트 파킹 시스템을 통해 차량 출입의 약 90%를 자동화하고 주차장 관리 인력의 업무를 70% 최적화했습니다. 또한, 사이트게이트(SiteGate)는 공항 건설 현장에 도입되어 인력 등록 및 신원 확인 절차의 디지털화를 지원하고 있습니다.

7월 말 현재, IOTek의 플랫폼은 9개 지역에 구축되어 5,000대 이상의 기기를 연결하고 61,000명 이상의 사용자에게 서비스를 제공하고 있습니다.

IOTek은 실용적인 응용 솔루션 개발 외에도 로봇 공학 및 디지털 트윈과 같은 신기술의 활용을 촉진하는 데 주력하고 있습니다. 또한, IOTek은 연구 활동을 통해 기술적 역량을 점차 입증하고 있으며, IOTek 부동산 관리, IOTek 스마트 주차, IOTek 스마트 시티 등 세 가지 솔루션에 대해 저작권 등록증을 획득했습니다.

IOTek은 향후 체계적인 전략을 바탕으로 IoT 플랫폼 및 AI 애플리케이션 연구 개발에 대한 투자를 지속적으로 확대하여 통합, 자동화 및 지능형 제어 기능을 강화하고, 공항 및 스마트 시티와 같은 대규모의 복잡한 스마트 인프라 프로젝트에 적용할 수 있도록 노력할 것입니다.

2014년에 시작된 '2026년 베트남 10대 디지털 기술 기업' 프로그램은 여러 차례에 걸쳐 약 800개 기업을 선정하며 베트남 디지털 기술 기업의 역량을 평가하고 기리는 대표적인 행사로 자리매김했습니다. 이 행사를 통해 기업들은 국내외 파트너 및 고객과 교류하고 관계를 구축할 수 있습니다.

출처: Vietnam.vn

item.title: IoT-Based Smart Street Lighting System Using ESP8266 - Hackster.io
item.description:
요약

  • Street lighting is an essential part of urban infrastructure, providing visibility and safety for pedestrians and vehicles.
  • To address this issue, we developed an IoT-Based Smart Street Lighting System using NodeMCU ESP8266, an LDR sensor, a PIR motion sensor, and an LED.
  • The system automatically controls street lighting based on surrounding light intensity and movement detection.

본문

Street lighting is an essential part of urban infrastructure, providing visibility and safety for pedestrians and vehicles. However, conventional street lighting systems often operate continuously during nighttime, regardless of whether anyone is present. This can result in unnecessary electricity consumption.

To address this issue, we developed an IoT-Based Smart Street Lighting System using NodeMCU ESP8266, an LDR sensor, a PIR motion sensor, and an LED.

The system automatically controls street lighting based on surrounding light intensity and movement detection. It also integrates with the KiwisIoT platform to enable remote monitoring of sensor readings and lighting status.

2. Project Objectives

The main objectives of this project are:

- Automate street light operation based on surrounding light conditions.

- Detect pedestrian movement using a PIR motion sensor.

- Automatically adjust LED brightness based on movement.

- Reduce unnecessary electricity consumption.

- Enable remote monitoring through the KiwisIoT platform.

- Demonstrate the practical implementation of IoT-based automation.

3. Hardware Components

The following hardware components are used to develop this project:

- NodeMCU ESP8266 – 1

- LDR Sensor Module – 1

- PIR Motion Sensor – 1

- 220Ω Resistor – 1

- Breadboard – 1

- Jumper Wires – As required

- USB Cable – 1

4. Software Requirements

- ESP8266 Board Package

- ESP8266WiFi Library

- KiwisIoT Library

- Embedded C/C++ Programming

5. Hardware Connections and ImplementationStep 1: Connecting the LDR Sensor

Connect the LDR sensor module to the NodeMCU ESP8266. The sensor measures the surrounding light intensity and helps identify daytime and nighttime conditions.

LDR Sensor Module → ESP8266

Sensor Pin ESP8266 Pin

The sensor continuously provides analog readings to the ESP8266 based on the surrounding light conditions.

Step 2: Connecting the PIR Motion Sensor

Connect the PIR motion sensor to the ESP8266 to detect pedestrian movement.

PIR Sensor → ESP8266

Sensor Pin ESP8266 Pin

VCC VIN / 5V (as supported by module)

OUT D5 (GPIO14)

When movement is detected, the PIR sensor sends a HIGH signal to the ESP8266. Otherwise, it provides a LOW signal after its configured detection period.

Step 3: Connecting the LED

Connect the LED to the ESP8266 to represent the street lighting system.

LED Pin ESP8266 Connection

Anode (+) D6 (GPIO12) through 220Ω resistor

Cathode (-) GND

The ESP8266 controls the LED brightness using PWM signals.

- During daytime, the LED remains OFF.

- During nighttime without movement, the LED operates at dim brightness.

- When movement is detected, the LED brightness increases.

Note: The direct LED connection is suitable for a small indicator LED. High-power street lights require an appropriate external driver circuit.

6. Programming and Configuration

The NodeMCU ESP8266 is programmed using the Arduino IDE.

item.title: How to make sure your smart home devices are secure from hackers - The Independent
item.description:
요약

  • How to make sure your smart home devices are secure from hackers
  • European supermarket fridges have been hit by mystery cyberattacks, leading to spoiled food and raising concerns about smart home devices
  • "The fridge will still operate as a regular refrigerator (cooling and freezing) without an internet connection, but you won’t have access to its advanced smart functions until it’s connected to your home network," the firm notes on its website.

본문

How to make sure your smart home devices are secure from hackers

European supermarket fridges have been hit by mystery cyberattacks, leading to spoiled food and raising concerns about smart home devices

Become an Independent member to bookmark this article

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Already a member? Log in

Recent cyber attacks targeting supermarket fridges across Europe destroyed vast quantities of food, leaving consumers questioning whether their own internet-connected household appliances could face similar threats.

Resembling a plot from science fiction, intruders manipulated commercial chilling systems into an endless defrost mode, driving internal temperatures up towards 50C.

These incidents underscored the rapid proliferation of everyday household items built with web connectivity. Although remote access offers convenience to individuals and operational efficiencies to firms, it inherently introduces new security risks.

How concerned should householders be regarding their smart appliances, and what measures can protect them?

How vulnerable are smart home devices?

The probability of a domestic smart appliance being breached remains "quite low for most people, but not zero," according to Mieke Verburgh, senior director of threat labs for Europe at the cyber security firm Malwarebytes.

"Nobody is likely to target you personally," Ms Verburgh explained, noting that users are far more liable to fall victim to automated scripts searching online for vulnerable targets—such as equipment running outdated software or relying on factory default settings.

Cyber security specialists indicate that criminals are unlikely to try causing domestic fridges to defrost. Instead, compromised devices are typically enlisted into botnets or harnessed to mask illicit web activity, such as online fraud, by making traffic appear to originate from a legitimate home address.

Appliance manufacturer Samsung stated that it is "fully committed to providing swift security updates for any identified vulnerabilities" and emphasised that its smart range features tailored security features designed to safeguard chipsets and software "under strict security standards."

item.title: Hierarchical Blockchain and Zero-Knowledge Architecture Cuts IoT Authentication Latency and Energy - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Connecting millions of microcontrollers to operational infrastructure requires verifying device identities without overwhelming embedded hardware or distributed networks.
  • In a study published in Results in Engineering, Haozhe Zhou, Hang Lei, and Maolin Yang introduced HybridTrust, a three-tier hierarchical architecture that coordinates physical unclonable functions, fog-level batch Bulletproofs, and cloud-level succinct zero-knowledge proofs.
  • The engineering team addressed this structural bottleneck by dividing authentication responsibilities across a computational gradient spanning devices, edge fog nodes, and cloud consensus infrastructure.

본문

Connecting millions of microcontrollers to operational infrastructure requires verifying device identities without overwhelming embedded hardware or distributed networks. In a study published in Results in Engineering, Haozhe Zhou, Hang Lei, and Maolin Yang introduced HybridTrust, a three-tier hierarchical architecture that coordinates physical unclonable functions, fog-level batch Bulletproofs, and cloud-level succinct zero-knowledge proofs. Evaluated across a heterogeneous testbed of 16 physical machines and up to 500 emulated containers representing up to 10,000 devices, the system achieved a mean end-to-end authentication latency of 160 to 220 milliseconds for offered loads up to 8,000 authentications per second and 240 milliseconds at 10,000 authentications per second. Across these loads, the architecture demonstrated an authentication throughput of up to 8,500 operations per second while requiring 0.3 millijoules of device-side energy per authentication event, reducing energy use by 92 percent compared to a public-key blockchain baseline and 94 percent compared to a per-device zero-knowledge baseline.

Industrial installations supporting automated manufacturing, smart transportation, and medical telemetry routinely supervise deployments containing between 100,000 and 1,000,000 heterogeneous microcontrollers. These deployed endpoints operate under stringent physical limitations, typically possessing roughly 100 kilobytes of random-access memory, 10 kilobytes of persistent storage, and strict power budgets that preclude intensive cryptographic operations. Conventional centralized systems frequently rely on gateway proxies or certificate authorities, yet standard gateways establish vulnerable centralized points of failure lacking verifiable evidence of authorization. Conversely, migrating authentication directly onto decentralized ledgers confronts what the investigators formalized as a security, scalability, and resource-efficiency trilemma: shared ledgers impose linear verification expenses when evaluating every device transaction independently, overwhelming both on-chain throughput and constrained microcontroller processors.

item.title: Study Quantifies Machine Learning Energy Costs Across Edge Computing Pipeline Stages - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Researchers Shravel Sharma, Imali Dias, and Kevin Lee have analyzed the energy costs of executing machine learning pipelines on edge computing hardware, deriving a formula to quantify energy consumption across distinct computing stages.
  • Machine learning computation is frequently performed directly on edge devices to improve the real-time responsiveness of Internet of Things systems.
  • However, these machine learning techniques demand considerable computational and energy resources, creating significant operational challenges in resource-constrained edge environments.

본문

Researchers Shravel Sharma, Imali Dias, and Kevin Lee have analyzed the energy costs of executing machine learning pipelines on edge computing hardware, deriving a formula to quantify energy consumption across distinct computing stages. Machine learning computation is frequently performed directly on edge devices to improve the real-time responsiveness of Internet of Things systems. However, these machine learning techniques demand considerable computational and energy resources, creating significant operational challenges in resource-constrained edge environments.

The study highlights that the increasing popularity of the Internet of Things has generated large volumes of data from connected devices. Machine learning techniques are regularly deployed to process this generated information, enabling networked systems to predict events and enhance automated decision-making. Because edge computing environments operate under strict resource constraints, managing the heavy computational workload required by these predictive algorithms is critical to maintaining continuous device operation.

To address these constraints, the researchers focused on evaluating the energy costs associated with different stages of the machine learning pipeline. The team examined energy usage across distinct operational steps, specifically analyzing data processing, model training, and inference across diverse hardware configurations. By assessing energy consumption across these pipeline stages under different model parameters, the work provides a foundation to improve technical understanding and support energy-efficient workflows on edge hardware.

A primary contribution of the research is the derivation of a mathematical formula designed to quantify the energy cost of an individual machine learning instance. This formula is developed to support energy-aware decision-making when designing and running computational tasks on edge systems. In addition to deriving the cost formula and evaluating pipeline stages, the authors conducted a comprehensive review of the current state of the art in energy-aware machine learning for edge computing.

According to the authors, the resulting pipeline evaluation and mathematical formula will guide the development of energy-aware machine learning solutions that optimize resource usage. By establishing clear metrics for energy consumption across varying hardware configurations and operational stages, the analysis provides a framework to enable sustainable and scalable Internet of Things applications that operate reliably within resource-constrained edge environments.

Subject of Research: Energy consumption of machine learning pipelines in edge computing

Article Title: The Energy Cost of Machine Learning in Edge Computing

Article References: Sharma, S., Dias, I., & Lee, K. (2026). The Energy Cost of Machine Learning in Edge Computing. International Journal of Networked and Distributed Computing. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44227-026-00139-7

item.title: Microsoft adds edge AI inference to Azure IoT Operations - IoT News
item.description:
요약

  • Microsoft has introduced new capabilities in Azure IoT Operations that allow industrial organisations to integrate AI inference into their data pipelines and give AI agents controlled access to factory information.
  • The features are part of Azure IoT Operations 2610. The release introduces a public preview channel alongside the generally available version, separating experimental AI capabilities from software intended for production environments.
  • While Azure IoT Operations includes capabilities for monitoring connected systems and data pipelines, Microsoft’s 2610 announcement does not detail a model-drift detection mechanism for the preview inference connector.

본문

Microsoft has introduced new capabilities in Azure IoT Operations that allow industrial organisations to integrate AI inference into their data pipelines and give AI agents controlled access to factory information.

The features are part of Azure IoT Operations 2610. The release introduces a public preview channel alongside the generally available version, separating experimental AI capabilities from software intended for production environments.

The update also introduces controls for managing how AI agents access operational systems. However, the new capabilities raise questions about processing performance, hardware requirements, and long-term model reliability.

Bringing AI inference to industrial systems

One of the main additions is an inference connector that allows Azure IoT Operations’ data pipelines to send requests to machine learning models and process their results. The connector supports models served locally through Microsoft’s Foundry Local and models hosted in Azure Machine Learning.

Industrial data can be sent to these models for processing, with the results made available to other applications or downstream workflows. The connector also supports larger inputs, including high-resolution images, by reading files from persistent storage instead of transmitting the full payload through the message broker.

Although the connector operates at the edge, not every supported model runs locally. Models hosted in Azure Machine Learning may require external connectivity, while locally deployed models can process data within a factory’s infrastructure. The choice affects network requirements and how inference workloads operate during connectivity interruptions.

Microsoft has also separated the 2610 release into two channels. The generally available version contains production-ready features, including improvements to industrial connectivity and data management. The preview channel adds capabilities such as AI inference, agent access to operational data, and additional application management functions.

According to Microsoft’s upgrade documentation, existing deployments cannot switch directly between the stable and preview channels. Organisations testing the new AI capabilities therefore need a separate preview installation rather than converting their existing production deployment. Microsoft also states that Azure IoT Operations does not support live upgrades, meaning operators should expect some downtime when updating their systems.

Controlling AI access to factory equipment

Alongside the inference connector, Microsoft has introduced a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in preview. The server allows compatible AI agents to access live operational telemetry and stored information through authenticated and authorised interfaces.

item.title: Signal Processing Framework Improves Windows Malware Detection by 1 to 6 Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • A novel malware detection framework converts operational code sequences into discrete numerical signals to identify threats targeting Windows Portable Executable and Internet of Things environments.
  • Addressing the rapid growth of Internet usage and the alarming increase in malware threats confronting digital systems worldwide, the methodology applies signal processing techniques directly to Opcode streams for feature extraction.
  • Subject of Research: Signal processing and entropy-based feature extraction for malware detection

본문

A novel malware detection framework converts operational code sequences into discrete numerical signals to identify threats targeting Windows Portable Executable and Internet of Things environments. Addressing the rapid growth of Internet usage and the alarming increase in malware threats confronting digital systems worldwide, the methodology applies signal processing techniques directly to Opcode streams for feature extraction. The researchers note that applying signal processing tools to Opcode sequences represents a first-time innovation that enables platform-independent malware detection.

To extract discriminative features from executable files, the framework analyzes overlapping sub-signals using a combination of entropy-based algorithms and fractal dimension methods. The entropy measures include Singular Value Decomposition Entropy, Permutation Entropy, and Spectral Entropy. These statistical metrics are paired with fractal dimension methods, including the Katz, Higuchi, and Petrosian algorithms.

Following feature extraction, the generated feature vectors are fed into a LightGBM classifier to perform binary classification between malware and benign samples. The researchers evaluated the framework across three separate datasets covering Windows Portable Executable files and Internet of Things samples. In these validation tests, the proposed architecture achieved classification accuracies of 94.65 percent, 93.99 percent, and 99.80 percent across the three datasets, respectively.

Assessments focused on the Windows dataset revealed that the framework achieved a 1 percent to 6 percent improvement over conventional approaches. This performance gain was demonstrated across multiple evaluation metrics, including precision, accuracy, recall, and F-measure.

Subject of Research: Signal processing and entropy-based feature extraction for malware detection

Article Title: Singular value decomposition entropy: An efficient feature for malware detection

Article References: Abazar, M., Alkhrijah, Y., Altulyan, M., Bin-Asfour, M., Mohammadi, M., Boostani, R., & Manavi, F. (2027). Singular value decomposition entropy: An efficient feature for malware detection. Cluster Computing, 30(1), Article 34. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10586-026-06794-3

DOI: 10.1007/s10586-026-06794-3

item.title: 제주대 스마트치유관광 MD, 추자도 신양2리 주민과 함께 IoT기반 마을 관광 정보 서비스 발굴 - 지금제주
item.description:
요약

  • 제주대학교(총장 양덕순) 관광경영학과 스마트치유관광 마이크로디그리(MD) 교육과정 수강생들이 추자도 신양2리 주민들과 함께 지역 고유의 관광자원을 활용한 스마트 관광 정보 서비스 발굴에 나섰다.
  • 지난 6일부터 7일까지 이뤄진 이번 답사는 사물인터넷 혁신융합대학사업 제주대사업단의 지원으로 마련됐으며 관광자행동론 교과목 수강생 48명과 인솔자 4명 등 총 52명이 참여해 지역 관광의 새로운 가능성을 탐색했다.
  • 학생들은 12개 팀으로 나뉘어 신양2리와 하추자도 일대를 답사하고, 관광객과 마을 주민을 대상으로 인터뷰를 진행하며 관광 과정에서 필요한 정보와 불편 사항을 세밀하게 살폈다.

본문

제주대학교(총장 양덕순) 관광경영학과 스마트치유관광 마이크로디그리(MD) 교육과정 수강생들이 추자도 신양2리 주민들과 함께 지역 고유의 관광자원을 활용한 스마트 관광 정보 서비스 발굴에 나섰다.

지난 6일부터 7일까지 이뤄진 이번 답사는 사물인터넷 혁신융합대학사업 제주대사업단의 지원으로 마련됐으며 관광자행동론 교과목 수강생 48명과 인솔자 4명 등 총 52명이 참여해 지역 관광의 새로운 가능성을 탐색했다.

학생들은 12개 팀으로 나뉘어 신양2리와 하추자도 일대를 답사하고, 관광객과 마을 주민을 대상으로 인터뷰를 진행하며 관광 과정에서 필요한 정보와 불편 사항을 세밀하게 살폈다. 이를 통해 관광객의 이동 동선과 정보 탐색 과정에서 나타나는 문제점을 파악하고, 실제 이용자의 관점에서 필요한 관광 서비스의 방향을 구체화했다.

신양2리 마을회관에서 열린 주민 워크숍에서는 학생들이 팀별 현장조사 결과를 공유하고, 주민들은 마을 관광자원의 활용과 관광 정보 제공에 관한 다양한 의견을 제시했다. 또한 주민들이 직접 관광 정보를 등록·갱신하는 등 마을 관광 서비스 운영에 주도적으로 참여할 수 있는 방안을 논의하며, 지역과 대학이 함께 만들어 가는 관광 정보 서비스의 가능성을 확인했다.

아울러 사물인터넷 혁신융합대학사업 제주대사업단과 신양2리 마을은 현장에서 업무협약(MOU)을 체결하고, 향후 마을 관광 관련 교육과 현장 프로젝트를 연계하기 위한 협력 기반을 마련했다.

학생들은 디자인 씽킹(Design Thinking) 과정을 거쳐 관광객의 요구와 주민 의견을 반영한 사물인터넷(IoT) 기반 마을 치유관광 정보 서비스를 기획하고, 모바일 웹 또는 앱 형태의 프로토타입을 구현할 예정이다. 이를 통해 관광객에게는 지역 관광 정보를 더욱 편리하게 제공하고, 주민에게는 마을 관광자원을 직접 관리하고 홍보할 수 있는 새로운 서비스 모델을 제안했다.

이번 답사를 통해 학생들은 강의실에서 배운 관광 이론을 실제 지역사회에 적용하고, 관광객과 주민의 관점에서 지역관광의 과제를 발견하는 현장 중심의 학습 경험을 쌓았다. 스마트치유관광 MD 교육과정은 앞으로도 지역사회와 지속적으로 협력해 스마트 기술과 지역 고유의 가치를 결합한 새로운 마을 치유관광 모델을 발굴해 나갈 계획이다.

오는 12월 9일에는 지산학프로젝트 결과보고회를 개최해 학생들이 기획한 관광 서비스 아이디어와 결과물을 공유할 예정이다. 이날 보고회에서는 하추자도 관계자가 직접 평가에 참여하며, 평가 결과 1위로 선정된 팀의 아이디어 또는 결과물은 하추자도에서 실제 활용할 계획이다. 이를 통해 학생들의 교육 성과가 지역 관광 현장에 적용되는 실질적인 지역·대학 협력 사례로 이어질 것으로 기대된다.

한편 사물인터넷 혁신융합대학사업은 대학과 학과 간 경계를 넘어 전공에 관계없이 학생들이 첨단 분야를 배울 수 있도록 여러 대학이 교육과정을 공동으로 개발·공유하는 사업이다. 제주대사업단은 교육부와 제주도의 지원을 바탕으로 제주도 및 제주대·제주한라대학교·세종대학교·동국대학교·대전대학교와 협력해 사업을 추진하고 있다.

출처: 지금제주

item.title: 이통3사 알뜰폰 자회사 점유율 ‘통신사별 50%’ 제한 추진…IoT 제외 - 매일경제
item.description:
요약

  • SK텔레콤, KT, LG유플러스 등 이동통신 3사 계열 알뜰폰 사업자의 시장점유율을 제한하는 법안이 발의됐다.
  • 국회 과학기술정보방송통신위원회 소속 무소속 최혁진 의원은 이동통신 3사 계열 알뜰폰 사업자의 시장점유율을 통신사별로 50% 이하로 제한하는 내용을 담은 전기통신사업법 일부개정법률안을 20일 발의했다고 밝혔다.
  • 개정안은 이통 3사 알뜰폰 자회사의 합산 점유율을 50%로 묶어둔 현행 규제 대신, 각 통신사가 망을 임대해 제공하는 알뜰폰 가입자 중 자사 계열 알뜰폰 가입자 비중이 50%를 넘지 못하도록 규정했다.

본문

SK텔레콤, KT, LG유플러스 등 이동통신 3사 계열 알뜰폰 사업자의 시장점유율을 제한하는 법안이 발의됐다.

국회 과학기술정보방송통신위원회 소속 무소속 최혁진 의원은 이동통신 3사 계열 알뜰폰 사업자의 시장점유율을 통신사별로 50% 이하로 제한하는 내용을 담은 전기통신사업법 일부개정법률안을 20일 발의했다고 밝혔다.

개정안은 이통 3사 알뜰폰 자회사의 합산 점유율을 50%로 묶어둔 현행 규제 대신, 각 통신사가 망을 임대해 제공하는 알뜰폰 가입자 중 자사 계열 알뜰폰 가입자 비중이 50%를 넘지 못하도록 규정했다.

점유율 산정 기준도 손질한다. 사물인터넷(IoT) 회선은 집계에서 제외하고 실제 이용자 중심의 휴대전화 회선만 반영하기로 했다. 만약 통신사별 자회사 점유율이 상한선인 50%를 초과할 경우 신규 가입자 모집을 중단하도록 하는 제재 조항도 포함됐다.

이번 입법은 기존 점유율 규제가 시장 현실을 반영하지 못해 대기업 계열 쏠림을 막는 데 한계가 있다는 지적에 따른 것이다. 올해 6월 기준 전체 알뜰폰 휴대전화 회선(1049만명) 가운데 이통 3사 계열사 가입자는 492만명으로 약 47%를 차지하고 있다.

알뜰폰 업계에서는 시장 균형을 맞추기 위한 제도 보완이 필요하다는 목소리가 나온다. 한 업계 관계자는 “대기업 자회사의 과도한 마케팅을 제어할 공정경쟁 장치가 필요하다”며 “중소 사업자들도 단순 저가 경쟁에서 벗어나 차별화된 경쟁력을 갖출 수 있도록 지원해야 한다”고 말했다.

최 의원은 “알뜰폰은 이동통신 3사의 과점을 견제하려고 만든 제도인데 가입자 두 명 중 한 명 가까이가 3사 계열사에 가입해 있다”며 “독립 중소 사업자가 같은 조건에서 경쟁할 수 있도록 끝까지 챙기겠다”고 밝혔다.

이번 법안에는 대표발의한 최혁진 의원을 포함해 김병기, 김우영, 김준형, 문진석, 서미화, 이수진, 이훈기, 장종태, 한준호 등 총 10명의 의원이 공동발의에 참여했다.

SK텔레콤이 망을 임대하는 알뜰폰 사업의 점유율 제한을 담은 전기통신사업법 개정안의 적용을 받습니다. 개정안은 자사 계열 알뜰폰 가입자 비중이 50%를 넘지 못하도록 규정하고 초과 시 신규 가입자 모집을 중단하도록 합니다. 규제 강화에 따른 영향이 나타나지만 실제 휴대전화 회선 중심의 공정경쟁 환경이 조성되는 반대급부도 있습니다.

이동통신 3사 계열 알뜰폰 사업자의 점유율을 통신사별 50%로 제한하는 법안이 발의되어 IoT 회선 제외 기준이 적용됩니다. 휴대전화 회선 중심의 점유율 산정 방식은 자사 계열 알뜰폰 가입자 비중을 통제하는 구조입니다. 알뜰폰 자회사의 신규 가입자 모집 제한은 부담이나 중소 사업자와의 경쟁 환경 변화를 동반합니다.

LG유플러스가 망을 제공하는 알뜰폰 영역에 계열사 가입자 50% 상한 규제가 추진됩니다. 법안은 이통 3사 계열 알뜰폰의 합산 점유율 규제 대신 통신사별 가입자 비중을 제한하는 방식입니다. 법안 심의 과정에서는 상한 산정과 제재 적용이 알뜰폰 경쟁 구도에 미칠 영향이 주요 쟁점으로 꼽힙니다.

최근 이동통신 3사 계열의 알뜰폰 사업자들을 겨냥한 새로운 시장점유율 제한 법안이 발의되면서 통신 시장의 이목이 집중되고 있어요. 📱💼 이번에 국회 과학기술정보방송통신위원회 소속 최혁진 의원을 비롯한 의원 10명이 전기통신사업법 일부개정법률안을 내놓았는데요. 📜 이 개정안은 기존의 헐렁했던 규제 틀을 다듬어 대기업 자회사로의 쏠림 현상을 막겠다는 의도를 담고 있어요. 🤔

기존에는 이통 3사 알뜰폰 자회사의 전체 합산 점유율을 50%로 묶어두는 방식이었지만, 이번 개정안은 각 통신사가 망을 빌려준 알뜰폰 가입자 중에서 '자사 계열 알뜰폰'이 차지하는 비중이 50%를 넘지 못하도록 기준을 구체적으로 바꿨어요. 📊 여기에 점유율을 계산할 때 사물인터넷(IoT) 회선은 제외하고, 오직 실제 사람이 사용하는 휴대전화 회선만 꼼꼼하게 따져서 반영하기로 했답니다. 📞 만약 통신사별 자회사 점유율이 상한선인 50%를 넘어가게 되면 신규 가입자를 아예 모집할 수 없도록 강력한 제재 조항도 함께 포함되었어요. 🚫
